tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate move legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before committing a move, check that the disk you intend to move is the topmost disk on its source peg and that the destination peg's top disk (if any) is larger than the moving disk. This prevents both non‑top moves and larger‑onto‑smaller violations.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you generate a move, verify these conditions before adding the move to the list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 3 from a peg where disk 2 is on top, resulting in a non‑top‑disk move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without breaking size constraints; use it to temporarily occupy a peg so that larger disks can be moved freely.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk is blocked by smaller disks on its source or target peg and you need a free peg to continue.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving the smallest disk on a peg while trying to move a larger disk from the same peg, causing the larger disk to be blocked.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains some of the largest disks in the correct order, keep them in place and build the rest of the tower on top of them.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the initial configuration already has a partial correct stack on the target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a correctly placed larger disk away from the target peg, even though it already matches the goal configuration.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Assemble the final tower by handling disks from largest to smallest, placing each disk onto the goal peg after clearing any smaller disks that block it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the final configuration, start with the largest missing disk and work downwards.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing a smaller disk onto the target peg before the larger missing disk, leading to later inability to place the larger disk.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the full sequence of moves, output it as the last syntactically correct list in the response, with no extra text after it. The verifier reads only the final parseable list.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the end of your answer, ensure the move list is the final structure presented.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing explanatory text after the move list, causing the parser to miss the moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear source and auxiliary pegs before moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you want to move has any smaller disks on top of it (on its source peg) or the auxiliary peg contains smaller disks that would interfere, move those smaller disks elsewhere first.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving a larger disk, ensure its source peg's top is that disk and the auxiliary peg does not block the move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 while disk 1 is still on top of it on the same peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg before placing a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk onto its final peg, ensure that the target peg does not have any smaller disks on top that would be violated by the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you are about to place a larger disk onto the goal peg, check that the top of the target peg is either empty or a larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 onto a peg where disk 2 is on top, resulting in a size ordering violation.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Alternate smallest-disk moves with the only other legal move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: In the classic three‑peg Hanoi, after each move of the smallest disk, the only other legal move (that does not involve the smallest) should be performed; this yields the optimal sequence of moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When solving a standard Hanoi sub‑problem where the smallest disk can be moved each turn.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving the smallest disk twice in a row without performing the required non‑smallest move, breaking the optimal pattern.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Limit move list length to stay within token limits
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a concise solution, preferably using the optimal or near‑optimal sequence of moves, to keep the answer within token limits.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the move list, avoid unnecessary extra moves that increase length without contributing to reaching the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including redundant moves that do not help reach the goal, making the answer overly long.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use target peg as temporary buffer for smallest disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When a larger disk is blocked on its source peg by smaller disks, move the smallest disk onto the target peg (if the target's top disk is larger) to free the source peg, then relocate the other smaller disks elsewhere, and finally move the smallest disk off the target before placing the larger disk onto the target. This prevents moving a non‑top disk and avoids larger‑onto‑smaller violations.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Applicable when you need to move a disk that is not currently top because smaller disks sit above it, and the target peg already contains smaller disks that would block the move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving the smallest disk back to its original peg instead of onto the target peg, which later forces a larger disk to be placed onto a smaller one.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop after reasoning or forget to output the final list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always include a move list as the last parseable structure in the answer.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model fails to check the destination peg's top disk before moving.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the destination peg's top disk (if any) is larger than the moving disk.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model does not track the current stack state correctly.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the disk you intend to move is the top disk on its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may run out of tokens or stop early.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Ensure the move list fully transforms the initial state to the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk from a peg where it is not present
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model loses track of disk locations.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain an up‑to‑date representation of each peg's contents before each move.
